reason: A genuine counterexample to the canonical assertion's own full-vector consistency conjunct. The canonical claim allows a proper subset with zero weights outside it and assumes neither full-vector identification nor additional mixture regularities. The fixed first component alone equals the true law; all (1,b) are true full vectors. The circle construction has an actual unique product-likelihood maximum for every positive finite sample, so it satisfies the unique-argmax convention as well. One estimator under one common IID law cannot converge in probability to all distinct (1,b). Refuting consistency suffices to refute the asserted conjunction with efficiency. The finite outcome and no-covariate specialization is a valid counterexample to the general claim, not a restriction of the refutation. Usual measurable-statistic conditions hold.

The canonical statement explicitly asserts asymptotic rejection probability at most alpha for the conventional added-variable OLS F test under IID sampling and conditional independence. The formal statement supplies alpha=1/2, genuine F(1,n-3) half-quantiles, the same conditional-independence null, and limiting rejection probability 1. Guarded rejection additionally requires full-rank regressions, positive residual risk and positive residual degrees of freedom, which eventually hold almost surely. A compatible full-support cell law has X uniform on {-1,0,1}, independent equiprobable Z given X, W=X^2+Z/2, and D conditionally Bernoulli with probabilities 3/4,1/4,3/4. W can be generated before treatment, and constant potential outcomes with these overlapping assignment probabilities also accommodate the causal setting. Neither linearity of the propensity nor homoskedastic regression errors is a hypothesis of the canonical size assertion.

The CP definition is the canonical absolute-error probability limit, sampleMean is the displayed arithmetic mean, IID has mutual independence and identical laws, and MemLp of order 2 on a probability space is finite second moment. With the standing existence of the mean this is equivalent to finite variance. Zero variance is expressly included by the canonical statement's footnote 10. No Chebyshev-rate conclusion from finite_lemmas is required as an additional audited clause.

Both the standardized and centered/scaled Gaussian limits are stated for the full IID finite-positive-variance domain. CD is exactly convergence of CDFs at continuity points. The standardized statistic uses the population mean and population standard deviation of the sample mean, as Definition 3.2.23 requires, rather than an estimated standard error. The finite identity between the two formulas and the stated standardization moments are also present. MemLp order 2 is equivalent to the printed finite mean and variance conditions, and the Gaussian parameter is variance.

The canonical statement itself includes the preceding sentence requiring a continuous PDF, so global continuity is retained rather than inferred only from its audit note. HasPDF correctly represents the common density, the rectangular kernel and estimator match Definition 3.3.7, and all deterministic positive bandwidth sequences with h->0 and n*h->infinity are covered. The conclusion is convergence in probability at every fixed real x. The n=0 conventions are immaterial to these limits.
